llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed file-based planning helper whose hooks, local files, optional session replay, and gated-stop behavior are purpose-aligned and locally scoped.

dimensions.detail: The skill uses local shell/Python/PowerShell helpers and environment variables for plan selection, cache paths, and host identity; this is proportionate to cross-platform planning hooks and no network upload path was found.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install surface is normal skill frontmatter plus bundled scripts/templates; hook path fallbacks look for this skill’s own known install paths rather than broadly enumerating or modifying other skills.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Lifecycle hooks inject selected project planning context into the model and remind the agent to update progress, but the artifact repeatedly frames injected content as untrusted data and documents opt-outs and selector behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It intentionally persists planning files, attestations, ledgers, counters, and private cache markers; optional gated mode can request stop blocking, but only when explicitly enabled and with documented caps and stall guards.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill’s purpose is persistent planning for long agent tasks, and its capabilities match that: it creates and reads task_plan.md, findings.md, progress.md, .planning state, ledgers, and local cache files.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want project planning files and lifecycle hooks that place selected planning context into the agent’s prompt. Avoid putting secrets in task_plan.md or progress.md, use --replay for session catchup only when you are comfortable surfacing prior same-project transcript excerpts, and enable gated mode only for tasks where stop-blocking behavior is desired.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: The referenced scripts and templates are present in the artifact; the scanner’s partial-inspection concern is downgraded because the package provides the referenced local files and they align with the documented planning workflow.
[TM1] expected: The flagged rm -f and mv -f operations target lock, temp, attestation, or mode-state files inside the selected plan/cache directories; they are cleanup/atomic-write mechanics, not destructive project-wide behavior.
[LP1] expected: The scripts read environment variables for configuration and inspect local session stores only through explicit catchup modes; the claimed network concern was not supported by artifact evidence of outbound requests or upload code.
[E4] expected: session-catchup.py can replay bounded same-project transcript excerpts, but SKILL.md discloses that --metadata emits counts only and --replay is explicit, bounded, nonce-framed, and treated as untrusted.
[AS3] expected: The hook command checks two fixed paths for this same skill’s skill-hook.sh as an install fallback; it does not list or read arbitrary peer skills.
